excerpt: State-level registration for shops, offices and commercial establishments, governing working hours, leave and employment conditions. Applied through the respective state labour department.

title: Import Export Code (IEC)
excerpt: Mandatory for any import or export business, issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade. One-time registration, valid for life of the entity.

title: Article 1: Name and territory of the Union

title: Article 2: Admission or establishment of new States
excerpt: Gives Parliament the power to admit new states into the Union or establish new states on such terms as it thinks fit (used when Sikkim joined in 1975). Such laws need only a simple majority.

title: Article 2A: Sikkim to be associated with the Union
excerpt: Inserted by the 35th Amendment 1975 giving Sikkim the special status of an associate state; omitted by the 36th Amendment 1975 when Sikkim became a full state of the Union.

title: Article 3: Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States
excerpt: Lets Parliament form a new state, increase or reduce a state's area, change its boundaries or rename it (used for state reorganisations like Andhra Pradesh/Telangana and the J and K reorganisation). Needs only a simple m

title: Article 4: Laws made under articles 2 and 3 to provide for the amendment of the First and the Fourth Schedules and supplemental, incidental and consequential matters
excerpt: Laws under Articles 2 and 3 may amend the First and Fourth Schedules and include consequential provisions; such laws are not treated as constitutional amendments under Article 368.

title: Article 5: Citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution
excerpt: Every person domiciled in India at the commencement of the Constitution (26 January 1950) who was born in India, or whose parents were born in India, or who had ordinarily lived in India for five years, became a citizen.

title: Article 6: Rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated to India from Pakistan
excerpt: Grants citizenship to persons who migrated to India from Pakistan: those who came before 19 July 1948 became citizens if resident since migration, while later migrants had to register with an appointed officer.

title: Article 7: Rights of citizenship of certain migrants to Pakistan
excerpt: Denies citizenship at commencement to anyone who migrated from India to Pakistan after 1 March 1947, except a person who returned to India under a permit for resettlement.

title: Article 8: Rights of citizenship of certain persons of Indian origin residing outside India
excerpt: Gives citizenship rights to a person of Indian origin residing outside India who registered as a citizen with an Indian diplomatic or consular representative.

title: Article 9: Persons voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign State not to be citizens
excerpt: Anyone who voluntarily acquires the citizenship of a foreign state automatically ceases to be an Indian citizen; India does not permit dual citizenship.

title: Article 10: Continuance of the rights of citizenship
excerpt: Every person who is a citizen under Part II continues to be one, subject to any law made by Parliament.

title: Article 11: Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law
excerpt: Empowers Parliament to make laws on acquisition and termination of citizenship; this is the constitutional basis of the Citizenship Act, 1955.

title: Article 12: Definition
excerpt: Defines 'the State' for Fundamental Rights: it includes the Government and Parliament of India, state governments and legislatures, and all local and other authorities (such as statutory bodies and public corporations) w

title: Article 13: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of the fundamental rights

title: Article 14: Equality before law

title: Article 15: Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth

title: Article 16: Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment
excerpt: Guarantees equality of opportunity in state employment and bars discrimination on religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth or residence. Clauses (4), (4A) and (4B) permit reservation for backward classes, SCs

title: Article 17: Abolition of Untouchability
excerpt: Abolishes untouchability in all forms and makes enforcing any disability arising from it a punishable offence (Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955). It is an absolute right available against private individuals as well.

title: Article 18: Abolition of titles
excerpt: Abolishes all titles except military and academic distinctions. Citizens cannot accept titles from foreign states, and foreigners holding offices of profit or trust need the President's consent to accept any foreign titl

title: Article 19: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
excerpt: Protects six freedoms: speech and expression, peaceful assembly without arms, forming associations or unions, free movement, residence and settlement, and practising any profession or trade. Each is subject to reasonable

title: Article 20: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
excerpt: Gives three criminal-justice safeguards: no ex post facto punishment (no conviction under a law made after the act), no double jeopardy (no second prosecution and punishment for the same offence), and no self-incriminati

title: Article 21: Protection of life and personal liberty
excerpt: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. After Maneka Gandhi (1978) this includes due process in substance, and the Court has read in rights to dignity, pr

title: Article 21A: Right to education
excerpt: Makes free and compulsory education a fundamental right for all children aged 6 to 14 (86th Amendment 2002), implemented through the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009.

title: Article 22: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
excerpt: An arrested person must be told the grounds of arrest, has the right to consult a lawyer, and must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours. Preventive detention is allowed with safeguards: detention beyond three

title: Article 23: Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
excerpt: Prohibits human trafficking, begar (forced unpaid labour) and other similar forms of forced labour, making violations punishable (Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976). The State may still impose compulsory public

title: Article 24: Prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.
excerpt: Bans employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or other hazardous work; the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016 extended the ban to all occupations for children below 14.

title: Article 25: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
excerpt: Every person may freely profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and other Fundamental Rights. The State may regulate secular activities linked to religion, and Sikhs' wearing o

title: Article 26: Freedom to manage religious affairs
excerpt: Every religious denomination may establish and maintain religious and charitable institutions, manage its own religious affairs, own and acquire property, and administer it according to law.

title: Article 27: Freedom as to payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion
excerpt: No person can be compelled to pay taxes whose proceeds are specifically used to promote or maintain any particular religion or religious denomination.

title: Article 28: Freedom as to attendance at religious instruction or religious worship in certain educational institutions
excerpt: Bars religious instruction in institutions wholly maintained by the State; in state-aided or recognised institutions, no person can be compelled to take part in religious instruction or worship without consent (or a guar

title: Article 29: Protection of interests of minorities
excerpt: Any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture may conserve it, and no citizen can be denied admission to state-maintained or aided educational institutions on grounds of religion, race, caste or lan

title: Article 30: Right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions
excerpt: Religious and linguistic minorities may establish and administer educational institutions of their choice, and the State cannot discriminate against them in granting aid (scope clarified in T.M.A. Pai, 2002).

title: Article 31: Compulsory acquisition of property
excerpt: Guaranteed the right to property as a fundamental right with compensation for acquisition; repealed by the 44th Amendment 1978, which moved property to Article 300A as a constitutional legal right.

title: Article 31A: Saving of laws providing for acquisition of estates, etc.
excerpt: Protects land-reform and estate-acquisition laws (like zamindari abolition) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19 (1st Amendment 1951); upheld in Kesavananda Bharati subject to the basic structure doctrine.

title: Article 31B: Validation of certain Acts and Regulations
excerpt: Validates the Acts listed in the Ninth Schedule against Fundamental Rights challenges; after I.R. Coelho (2007), laws inserted into the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 remain open to basic-structure review.

title: Article 31C: Saving of laws giving effect to certain directive principles
excerpt: Protects laws implementing Articles 39(b) and 39(c) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19; the 42nd Amendment's wider version was struck down in Minerva Mills (1980), leaving the original narrow form intact.

title: Article 32: Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part
excerpt: Gives every person the right to move the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights; Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution. The Court may issue the writs of habeas corpus, mandamus,

title: Article 33: Power of Parliament to modify the rights conferred by this Part in their application to Forces, etc.
excerpt: Empowers Parliament to restrict Fundamental Rights of members of the armed forces, paramilitary forces, police and intelligence agencies to maintain discipline (Army Act, 1950 and similar laws).

title: Article 34: Restriction on rights conferred by this Part while martial law is in force in any area
excerpt: Lets Parliament indemnify public servants for acts done to maintain order during martial law and validate their sentences; only Parliament, not state legislatures, may make such a law.

title: Article 35: Legislation to give effect to the provisions of this Part
excerpt: Reserves to Parliament (excluding state legislatures) the power to make laws giving effect to specified Fundamental Rights and to prescribe punishments for acts declared offences under this Part.

title: Article 36: Definition
excerpt: Defines 'the State' for the Directive Principles with the same meaning as in Article 12.

title: Article 37: Application of the principles contained in this Part
excerpt: The Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country and the State must apply them while making laws.

title: Article 38: State to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people
excerpt: Directs the State to secure a social order with justice (social, economic and political) informing all institutions, and to minimise inequalities of income, status, facilities and opportunities (second clause added by th

title: Article 39: Certain principles of policy to be followed by the State
excerpt: Lays down policy goals: adequate means of livelihood for all, ownership and control of material resources for the common good, no concentration of wealth, equal pay for equal work, protection of workers' health and stren

title: Article 39A: Equal justice and free legal aid
excerpt: Directs the State to provide free legal aid so that justice is not denied for economic reasons (42nd Amendment 1976); implemented through the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 and NALSA.

title: Article 40: Organisation of village panchayats
excerpt: Directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government; given constitutional shape by the 73rd Amendment 1992 (Part IX).

title: Article 41: Right to work, to education and to public assistance in certain cases
excerpt: Directs the State to secure the right to work, to education and to public assistance in unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement, within the limits of its economic capacity.

title: Article 42: Provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief
excerpt: Directs the State to secure just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief for women workers (basis of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961).

title: Article 43: Living wage, etc., for workers
excerpt: Directs the State to secure a living wage, decent conditions of work and leisure for workers, and to promote cottage industries in rural areas.

title: Article 43A: Participation of workers in management of industries
excerpt: Directs the State to secure workers' participation in the management of industrial undertakings (42nd Amendment 1976).

title: Article 43B: Promotion of co-operative societies
excerpt: Directs the State to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control and professional management of co-operative societies (97th Amendment 2011).

title: Article 44: Uniform civil code for the citizens
excerpt: Directs the State to secure a uniform civil code for all citizens; discussed in Shah Bano (1985) and ongoing personal-law debates. Uttarakhand enacted a state UCC in 2024.

title: Article 45: Provision for early childhood care and education to children below the age of six years
excerpt: Directs the State to provide early childhood care and education for children below six (as substituted by the 86th Amendment 2002; the earlier free-compulsory-education mandate became the fundamental right in Article 21A

title: Article 46: Promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections
excerpt: Directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections with special care, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation.

title: Article 47: Duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health
excerpt: Makes raising nutrition, living standards and public health a primary duty of the State, and directs it to endeavour to prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health.

title: Article 48: Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry
excerpt: Directs the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and to prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves and other milch and draught cattle.

title: Article 48A: Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wild life
excerpt: Directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife (42nd Amendment 1976).

title: Article 49: Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance
excerpt: Makes it the State's duty to protect every monument, place or object of artistic or historic interest declared of national importance from spoliation, disfigurement and destruction.

title: Article 50: Separation of judiciary from executive
excerpt: Directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services (the basis of an independent subordinate judiciary).

title: Article 51: Promotion of international peace and security
excerpt: Directs the State to promote international peace and security, maintain just and honourable relations between nations, foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and encourage settlement of internationa

title: Article 51A: Fundamental duties
excerpt: Lists eleven duties of every citizen: respect the Constitution, cherish the ideals of the freedom struggle, protect India's sovereignty and integrity, defend the country, promote harmony and brotherhood, preserve the com

title: Article 52: The President of India
excerpt: There shall be a President of India, the head of state and formal executive head of the Union.

title: Article 53: Executive power of the Union
excerpt: Vests the Union's executive power in the President, exercisable directly or through subordinate officers; the President is also the supreme commander of the defence forces.

title: Article 54: Election of President
excerpt: The President is elected by an electoral college of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected MLAs of the states (including Delhi and Puducherry), not by direct popular vote.

title: Article 55: Manner of election of President
excerpt: Prescribes proportional representation by single transferable vote with secret ballot; each MLA's vote value is weighted by state population so that all states have uniform weight.

title: Article 56: Term of office of President
excerpt: The President holds office for five years, may resign by writing to the Vice-President, may be removed by impeachment, and continues until a successor takes over.

title: Article 57: Eligibility for re-election
excerpt: A person who holds or has held the office of President is eligible for re-election; there is no term limit.

title: Article 58: Qualifications for election as President
excerpt: A candidate must be an Indian citizen, at least 35 years old, qualified for election to the Lok Sabha, and must not hold any office of profit.

title: Article 59: Conditions of President's office
excerpt: The President cannot be an MP or MLA, cannot hold any other office of profit, and is entitled to fixed emoluments, allowances and privileges during the term.

title: Article 60: Oath or affirmation by the President
excerpt: The President takes an oath to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law, administered by the Chief Justice of India (or the senior-most SC judge available).

title: Article 61: Procedure for impeachment of the President
excerpt: Impeachment charges may be preferred by either House with signatures of one-fourth of its members and 14 days' notice, and must be passed by a two-thirds majority of the total membership of each House; the President may

title: Article 62: Time of holding election to fill vacancy in the office of President and the term of office of person elected to fill casual vacancy
excerpt: An election to fill a Presidential vacancy must be held within six months; a person elected to a casual vacancy serves a full five-year term.

title: Article 63: The Vice-President of India
excerpt: There shall be a Vice-President of India, the second-highest constitutional office in the country.

title: Article 64: The Vice-President to be ex officio Chairman of the Council of States
excerpt: The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and does not vote except to break a tie as the presiding officer.

title: Article 65: The Vice-President to act as President or to discharge his functions during casual vacancies in the office, or during the absence, of President
excerpt: The Vice-President acts as President during a vacancy or the President's temporary absence; when acting during a vacancy, a new President must be elected within six months.

title: Article 66: Election of Vice-President
excerpt: The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of all members (elected and nominated) of both Houses of Parliament, by proportional representation with single transferable vote.

title: Article 67: Term of office of Vice-President
excerpt: The Vice-President holds office for five years; may be removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by a majority of all its members and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, with at least 14 days' notice.

title: Article 68: Time of holding election to fill vacancy in the office of Vice-President and the term of office of person elected to fill casual vacancy
excerpt: An election to fill a Vice-Presidential vacancy is held as soon as possible after the vacancy; a person elected to a casual vacancy serves a full five-year term.

title: Article 69: Oath or affirmation by the Vice-President
excerpt: The Vice-President takes the oath of office before the President (or a person appointed by the President).

title: Article 70: Discharge of President's functions in other contingencies
excerpt: Parliament may provide for discharge of the President's functions in contingencies not covered elsewhere; under the 1969 Act, the CJI (then the senior-most SC judge) discharges the functions.

title: Article 71: Matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President
excerpt: Disputes about the election of the President or Vice-President are decided only by the Supreme Court, whose decision is final; Parliament may regulate related matters by law.

title: Article 72: Power of President to grant pardons, etc., and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases
excerpt: Gives the President power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions and commutations in court-martial cases, offences against Union laws, and all death sentences; this power is wider than the Governor's under Art

title: Article 73: Extent of executive power of the Union
excerpt: The Union's executive power extends to matters on which Parliament can legislate and to the exercise of treaty rights, but not into the states' exclusive legislative field except as the Constitution provides.

title: Article 74: Council of Ministers to aid and advise President
excerpt: There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall act in accordance with that advice; the President may require the Council to reconsider its advice once

title: Article 75: Other provisions as to Ministers
excerpt: The Prime Minister is appointed by the President and other ministers on the PM's advice; ministers hold office during the President's pleasure; the Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha; a minister must be

title: Article 76: Attorney-General for India
excerpt: The President appoints the Attorney-General, the Union government's chief legal adviser, who must be qualified to be an SC judge; the AG has the right of audience in all courts and may take part in Parliament without vot

title: Article 77: Conduct of business of the Government of India
excerpt: All executive action of the Government of India is taken in the President's name; the President makes rules for the convenient transaction of business and its allocation among ministers.

title: Article 78: Duties of Prime Minister as respects the furnishing of information to the President, etc.
excerpt: It is the Prime Minister's duty to communicate Council of Ministers decisions and legislative proposals to the President, furnish information the President calls for, and submit for the Council's consideration any matter

title: Article 79: Constitution of Parliament
excerpt: Parliament consists of the President, the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

title: Article 80: Composition of the Council of States
excerpt: The Rajya Sabha has up to 250 members: 238 representing states and Union Territories (elected by MLAs by proportional representation) and 12 nominated by the President from literature, science, art and social service; it

title: Article 81: Composition of the House of the People
excerpt: The Lok Sabha has up to 552 members (530 from states, 20 from Union Territories, plus 2 formerly nominated Anglo-Indians, now omitted); members are directly elected by the people; its normal term is five years.

title: Article 82: Readjustment after each census
excerpt: After every census, Parliament readjusts Lok Sabha seat allocation and constituency delimitation by law; the 84th Amendment froze this on the 1971 census figures until after 2026.

title: Article 83: Duration of Houses of Parliament
excerpt: The Rajya Sabha is a continuing body with one-third of members retiring every two years; the Lok Sabha's normal duration is five years unless dissolved sooner, extendable by one year at a time during a National Emergency

title: Article 84: Qualification for membership of Parliament
excerpt: To be an MP a person must be an Indian citizen, at least 30 years old for the Rajya Sabha and 25 for the Lok Sabha, and possess other qualifications prescribed by Parliament (Representation of the People Act, 1951).

title: Article 85: Sessions of Parliament, prorogation and dissolution
excerpt: The President summons each House (the gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months), may prorogue the Houses, and may dissolve the Lok Sabha.

title: Article 86: Right of President to address and send messages to Houses
excerpt: The President may address either House of Parliament or both Houses together, and may send messages on Bills pending in Parliament.

title: Article 87: Special address by the President
excerpt: The President addresses both Houses assembled together at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year, laying out the government's policy agenda.

title: Article 88: Rights of Ministers and Attorney-General as respects Houses
excerpt: Every minister and the Attorney-General may speak and take part in the proceedings of either House and its committees, but may vote only in the House of which they are members.

title: Article 89: The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States
excerpt: The Vice-President is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; the House elects a Deputy Chairman from among its members.

title: Article 90: Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the office of Deputy Chairman
excerpt: The Deputy Chairman vacates office on ceasing to be a Rajya Sabha member, by resigning to the Chairman, or by removal through a resolution passed by a majority of all members of the House.

title: Article 91: Power of the Deputy Chairman or other person to perform the duties of the office of, or to act as, Chairman
excerpt: The Deputy Chairman (or a member fixed by the rules, or a person appointed by the President) performs the Chairman's duties during a vacancy or absence.

title: Article 92: The Chairman or the Deputy Chairman not to preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration
excerpt: The Chairman or Deputy Chairman must vacate the chair while a resolution for their removal is under consideration, though they may be present; the Chairman may vote only to break a tie.

title: Article 93: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People
excerpt: The Lok Sabha chooses two of its members as Speaker and Deputy Speaker, as soon as possible after it is constituted.

title: Article 94: Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker
excerpt: The Speaker or Deputy Speaker vacates office on ceasing to be an MP, by resignation, or by removal through a Lok Sabha resolution passed by a majority of all members with at least 14 days' notice.

title: Article 95: Power of the Deputy Speaker or other person to perform the duties of the office of, or to act as, Speaker
excerpt: The Deputy Speaker (or a member fixed by the rules, or a person chosen by the House) performs the Speaker's duties during a vacancy or absence.

title: Article 96: The Speaker or the Deputy Speaker not to preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration
excerpt: The Speaker or Deputy Speaker must vacate the chair while their own removal resolution is considered, but unlike the Rajya Sabha Chairman they may vote in the first instance.

title: Article 97: Salaries and allowances of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker
excerpt: Their salaries and allowances are fixed by Parliament by law and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

title: Article 98: Secretariat of Parliament
excerpt: Each House of Parliament has its own separate secretariat, with Parliament regulating their recruitment and service conditions by law.

title: Article 99: Oath or affirmation by members
excerpt: Every MP must take an oath or affirmation in the Third Schedule form before taking a seat in Parliament.

title: Article 100: Voting in Houses, power of Houses to act notwithstanding vacancies and quorum
excerpt: Decisions are taken by a majority of members present and voting (the presiding officer votes only on a tie); a House may act despite vacancies; quorum is one-tenth of the House's total membership.

title: Article 101: Vacation of seats
excerpt: An MP's seat falls vacant on disqualification under Article 102, on resignation, on 60 days' absence without permission, or on holding both Houses' seats; the House may declare the seat vacant.

title: Article 102: Disqualifications for membership
excerpt: Disqualified if the person holds an office of profit, is of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, is not an Indian citizen or has voluntarily acquired foreign citizenship, or is disqualified under any Parliamentary

title: Article 103: Decision on questions as to disqualifications of members
excerpt: The President decides disqualification questions under Article 102, in accordance with the Election Commission's opinion.

title: Article 104: Penalty for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation under article 99 or when not qualified or when disqualified
excerpt: An unqualified person who sits or votes in Parliament is liable to a fine of five hundred rupees for each day.

title: Article 105: Powers, privileges, etc., of the Houses of Parliament and of the members and committees thereof
excerpt: MPs enjoy freedom of speech in Parliament, immunity from court proceedings for votes and speeches, and the House's powers and privileges as defined by Parliament (key cases: Keshav Singh, JMM bribery case).

title: Article 106: Salaries and allowances of members
excerpt: MPs' salaries and allowances are fixed by Parliament by law.

title: Article 107: Provisions as to introduction and passing of Bills
excerpt: A Bill may originate in either House (except Money Bills); it must be passed by both Houses and receive the President's assent to become law; a Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on dissolution.

title: Article 108: Joint sitting of both Houses in certain cases
excerpt: If the Houses disagree on a Bill, the President may summon a joint sitting (except for Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills); the decision is by a majority of those present and voting (used in 1961, 1978 and 2002

title: Article 109: Special procedure in respect of Money Bills
excerpt: Money Bills may be introduced only in the Lok Sabha on the President's recommendation; the Rajya Sabha has 14 days to recommend amendments, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

title: Article 110: Definition of "Money Bills"
excerpt: A Bill is a Money Bill only if it deals exclusively with taxation, borrowing, the Consolidated or Contingency Funds, appropriation, or audit and accounts (the Aadhaar Act's Money Bill certification was litigated in Rojer

title: Article 111: Assent to Bills
excerpt: The President may assent to a Bill, withhold assent, or return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration; on reconsideration and re-passing, the President must assent (used for the office-of-profit Bill in 2006).

title: Article 112: Annual financial statement
excerpt: The President causes the Annual Financial Statement (the Union Budget) to be laid before Parliament each year, showing estimated receipts and expenditure.

title: Article 113: Procedure in Parliament with respect to estimates
excerpt: Estimates are presented as demands for grants voted by the Lok Sabha; no demand can be made without the President's recommendation.

title: Article 114: Appropriation Bills
excerpt: After grants are voted, an Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet those grants; no amendment varying the amount is allowed.

title: Article 115: Supplementary, additional or excess grants
excerpt: The President may lay before Parliament supplementary, additional or excess demands when authorised expenditure proves insufficient or money is spent beyond the grant.

title: Article 116: Votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants
excerpt: The Lok Sabha may grant a vote on account in advance pending the budget, votes of credit for indefinite demands, and exceptional grants outside the normal service of the year.

title: Article 117: Special provisions as to financial Bills
excerpt: Financial Bills of category I and II follow special procedures; Bills like Money Bills need the President's prior recommendation and cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.

title: Article 118: Rules of procedure
excerpt: Each House of Parliament makes its own rules of procedure and conduct of business.

title: Article 119: Regulation by law of procedure in Parliament in relation to financial business
excerpt: Parliament may by law regulate its financial-business procedure to ensure timely completion of financial business.

title: Article 120: Language to be used in Parliament
excerpt: Business is transacted in Hindi or English; after 15 years from commencement, English could be dropped unless Parliament provided otherwise, and Parliament has continued it (Official Languages Act, 1963).

title: Article 121: Restriction on discussion in Parliament
excerpt: No discussion may take place in Parliament about the conduct of any Supreme Court or High Court judge in the discharge of duties, except on a motion for removal (Article 124(4)).

title: Article 122: Courts not to inquire into proceedings of Parliament
excerpt: Courts cannot question the validity of Parliamentary proceedings for alleged irregularity of procedure (this protects internal proceedings, not illegal unconstitutional acts).

title: Article 123: Power of President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament
excerpt: The President may promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session if immediate action is needed; an ordinance has the force of law but must be laid before Parliament and lapses six weeks after reassembly (R.C. Co

title: Article 124: Establishment and constitution of Supreme Court
excerpt: Establishes the Supreme Court of India with a Chief Justice and up to 33 other judges (originally 7, raised by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act); judges are appointed by the President under the collegium system (

title: Article 125: Salaries, etc., of Judges
excerpt: Supreme Court judges' salaries and allowances are fixed by Parliament by law and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; they cannot be varied to a judge's disadvantage.

title: Article 126: Appointment of acting Chief Justice
excerpt: When the Chief Justice's office is vacant or the CJI is absent or unable to perform duties, the President appoints another SC judge as acting Chief Justice.

title: Article 127: Appointment of ad hoc judges
excerpt: The Chief Justice, with the President's prior consent, may request a High Court judge qualified for the SC to sit as an ad hoc judge when the Court lacks quorum.

title: Article 128: Attendance of retired Judges at sittings of the Supreme Court
excerpt: The Chief Justice, with the President's prior consent, may request a retired SC or High Court judge to sit and act as a judge of the Supreme Court.

title: Article 129: Supreme Court to be a court of record
excerpt: The Supreme Court is a court of record with the power to punish for its own contempt (Contempt of Courts Act, 1971).

title: Article 130: Seat of Supreme Court
excerpt: The Supreme Court sits in Delhi; the Chief Justice, with the President's approval, may appoint other places for sittings.

title: Article 131: Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
excerpt: The Supreme Court has exclusive original jurisdiction over disputes between the Union and states or between states (used in inter-state disputes like the Cauvery matter).

title: Article 131A: Exclusive jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in regard to questions as to constitutional validity of Central laws
excerpt: Inserted by the 42nd Amendment 1976 giving the SC exclusive jurisdiction over the constitutional validity of central laws; omitted by the 43rd Amendment 1977.

title: Article 132: Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in appeals from High Courts in certain cases
excerpt: An appeal lies to the Supreme Court from a High Court judgment involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, on the High Court's certificate.

title: Article 133: Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in appeals from High Courts in regard to civil matters
excerpt: An appeal lies in civil matters on the High Court's certificate that the case involves a substantial question of law of general importance needing the Supreme Court's decision.

title: Article 134: Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court in regard to criminal matters
excerpt: An appeal lies in criminal matters where the High Court reversed an acquittal and sentenced to death, withdrew a case to itself and sentenced to death, or certifies the case fit for appeal.

title: Article 134A: Certificate for appeal to the Supreme Court
excerpt: Every High Court passing or making a judgment, decree, final order or sentence must consider whether to grant a certificate for appeal to the Supreme Court (42nd Amendment 1976).

title: Article 135: Jurisdiction and powers of the Federal Court under existing law to be exercisable by the Supreme Court
excerpt: The Supreme Court exercises the jurisdiction and powers of the former Federal Court under pre-Constitution laws until Parliament provides otherwise.

title: Article 136: Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court
excerpt: The Supreme Court may in its discretion grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree or order of any court or tribunal in India (not applying to armed forces tribunals).

title: Article 137: Review of judgments or orders by the Supreme Court
excerpt: The Supreme Court may review its own judgments or orders, subject to Parliamentary law and its own rules (review petitions, and curative petitions after Rupa Ashok Hurra, 2002).

title: Article 138: Enlargement of the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
excerpt: Parliament may by law enlarge the Supreme Court's jurisdiction and powers with respect to matters in the Union List, and by special agreement for other matters.

title: Article 139: Conferment on the Supreme Court of powers to issue certain writs
excerpt: Parliament may confer on the Supreme Court power to issue writs (other than for Fundamental Rights, covered by Article 32) for any other purpose.

title: Article 139A: Transfer of certain cases
excerpt: The Supreme Court may transfer cases involving the same or substantially the same question of law pending before it and one or more High Courts to itself, or transfer cases between High Courts (42nd Amendment 1976).

title: Article 140: Ancillary powers of Supreme Court
excerpt: Parliament may confer supplementary powers on the Supreme Court to make its jurisdiction effective.

title: Article 141: Law declared by Supreme Court to be binding on all courts
excerpt: The law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts in India (the doctrine of precedent; Article 141 underpins stare decisis).

title: Article 142: Enforcement of decrees and orders of Supreme Court and orders as to discovery, etc.
excerpt: The Supreme Court may pass any decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in a case (Article 142's 'complete justice' power), enforceable throughout India.

title: Article 143: Power of President to consult Supreme Court
excerpt: The President may refer questions of law or fact of public importance to the Supreme Court for its advisory opinion, which is not binding (used in the Ayodhya reference and the 2G reference).

title: Article 144: Civil and judicial authorities to act in aid of the Supreme Court
excerpt: All civil and judicial authorities in India must act in aid of the Supreme Court.

title: Article 145: Rules of Court, etc.
excerpt: The Supreme Court makes rules regulating its practice and procedure, subject to Parliamentary law and the President's approval.

title: Article 146: Officers and servants and the expenses of the Supreme Court
excerpt: The Chief Justice appoints the Court's officers and servants; administrative expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

title: Article 147: Interpretation
excerpt: Defines 'a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of this Constitution' and related expressions used in this Chapter.

title: Article 148: Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
excerpt: There shall be a Comptroller and Auditor-General of India appointed by the President, removable only like an SC judge, who audits the accounts of the Union and the states.

title: Article 149: Duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
excerpt: The CAG performs duties and exercises powers prescribed by Parliament (CAG's (DPC) Act, 1971), covering Union, state and public-sector accounts.

title: Article 150: Form of accounts of the Union and of the States
excerpt: The Union and state accounts are kept in the form prescribed by the President on the CAG's advice.

title: Article 151: Audit reports
excerpt: The CAG's reports on Union accounts go to the President, who lays them before Parliament; state reports go to the Governor for the state legislature.

title: Article 152: Definition
excerpt: For this Part, 'State' does not include Jammu and Kashmir as originally framed; after the 2019 reorganisation the definition's application changed accordingly.

title: Article 153: Governors of States
excerpt: There shall be a Governor for each state; one person may be appointed Governor of two or more states.

title: Article 154: Executive power of State
excerpt: Vests the state's executive power in the Governor, exercisable directly or through subordinate officers.

title: Article 155: Appointment of Governor
excerpt: The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

title: Article 156: Term of office of Governor
excerpt: The Governor holds office for five years but serves during the President's pleasure, may resign to the President, and continues until a successor takes over.

title: Article 157: Qualifications for appointment as Governor
excerpt: A person must be an Indian citizen and at least 35 years old to be appointed Governor.

title: Article 158: Conditions of Governor's office
excerpt: The Governor cannot be an MP or MLA, cannot hold any other office of profit, and is entitled to fixed emoluments, allowances and privileges.

title: Article 159: Oath or affirmation by the Governor
excerpt: The Governor takes an oath to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution, administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court (or the senior-most judge available).

title: Article 160: Discharge of the functions of the Governor in certain contingencies
excerpt: The President may make provisions for discharge of the Governor's functions in contingencies not provided for in this Chapter.

title: Article 161: Power of Governor to grant pardons, etc., and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases
excerpt: The Governor may grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions and commutations in state-law offences, but has no power over death sentences (unlike the President under Article 72).

title: Article 162: Extent of executive power of State
excerpt: The state's executive power extends to matters on which the state legislature can legislate.

title: Article 163: Council of Ministers to aid and advise Governor
excerpt: There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor, who acts on that advice except where the Constitution requires discretion (position clarified by the 42nd and 44th

title: Article 164: Other provisions as to Ministers
excerpt: The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor and other ministers on the CM's advice; ministers hold office during the Governor's pleasure; the Council is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly; total min

title: Article 165: Advocate-General for the State
excerpt: The Governor appoints the Advocate-General, the state's chief legal adviser, who must be qualified to be a High Court judge and has the right of audience in all courts in the state.

title: Article 166: Conduct of business of the Government of a State
excerpt: All executive action of a state government is taken in the Governor's name; the Governor makes rules for the transaction of business and its allocation among ministers.

title: Article 167: Duties of Chief Minister as respects the furnishing of information to Governor, etc.
excerpt: The Chief Minister must communicate Council of Ministers decisions and legislative proposals to the Governor, furnish information the Governor calls for, and submit for the Council's consideration any matter decided by a

title: Article 168: Constitution of Legislatures in States
excerpt: Every state has a legislature of the Governor plus either two Houses (Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council) or one House; six states currently have Councils: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telanga

title: Article 169: Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in States
excerpt: Parliament may by law abolish or create a Legislative Council in a state if the state's Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority; such laws need only a simple majority in Parliament.

title: Article 170: Composition of the Legislative Assemblies
excerpt: An Assembly has between 60 and 500 members directly elected from territorial constituencies; each state is divided into constituencies so that the population-to-seat ratio is broadly uniform.

title: Article 171: Composition of the Legislative Councils
excerpt: A Legislative Council has up to one-third of the Assembly's strength (minimum 40); members are elected by local bodies, graduates, teachers and MLAs, with the rest nominated by the Governor from distinguished fields.

title: Article 172: Duration of State Legislatures
excerpt: An Assembly's normal duration is five years unless dissolved sooner, extendable by one year at a time during a National Emergency; the Council is a continuing body with one-third retiring every two years.

title: Article 173: Qualification for membership of the State Legislature
excerpt: To be an MLA or MLC a person must be an Indian citizen, at least 25 years old for the Assembly and 30 for the Council, and possess other qualifications prescribed by Parliament.

title: Article 174: Sessions of the State Legislature, prorogation and dissolution
excerpt: The Governor summons each House (the gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months), may prorogue the Houses, and may dissolve the Assembly.

title: Article 175: Right of Governor to address and send messages to the House or Houses
excerpt: The Governor may address the legislature and send messages on Bills, which the House must consider.

title: Article 176: Special address by the Governor
excerpt: The Governor addresses the legislature at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year.

title: Article 177: Rights of Ministers and Advocate-General as respects the Houses
excerpt: Every minister and the Advocate-General may speak and take part in either House's proceedings and committees, but may vote only in the House of which they are members.

title: Article 178: The Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
excerpt: The Assembly chooses two of its members as Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

title: Article 179: Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker
excerpt: The Speaker or Deputy Speaker vacates office on ceasing to be an MLA, by resignation, or by removal through an Assembly resolution passed by a majority of all members with at least 14 days' notice.

title: Article 180: Power of the Deputy Speaker or other person to perform the duties of the office of, or to act as, Speaker
excerpt: The Deputy Speaker (or a member fixed by the rules) performs the Speaker's duties during a vacancy or absence.

title: Article 181: The Speaker or the Deputy Speaker not to preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration
excerpt: The Speaker or Deputy Speaker must vacate the chair while their own removal resolution is considered, but may vote in the first instance.

title: Article 182: The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council
excerpt: The Council chooses a Chairman and Deputy Chairman from among its members.

title: Article 183: Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of Chairman and Deputy Chairman
excerpt: The Chairman or Deputy Chairman vacates office on ceasing to be an MLC, by resignation, or by removal through a Council resolution passed by a majority of all members.

title: Article 184: Power of the Deputy Chairman or other person to perform the duties of the office of, or to act as, Chairman
excerpt: The Deputy Chairman (or a member fixed by the rules) performs the Chairman's duties during a vacancy or absence.

title: Article 185: The Chairman or the Deputy Chairman not to preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration
excerpt: The Chairman or Deputy Chairman must vacate the chair while their own removal resolution is considered, though they may be present.

title: Article 186: Salaries and allowances of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker and the Chairman and Deputy Chairman
excerpt: Their salaries and allowances are fixed by the state legislature by law and charged on the state's Consolidated Fund.

title: Article 187: Secretariat of State Legislature
excerpt: Each House of a state legislature has its own separate secretariat, with the legislature regulating recruitment and service conditions by law.

title: Article 188: Oath or affirmation by members
excerpt: Every MLA or MLC must take an oath or affirmation in the Third Schedule form before taking a seat.

title: Article 189: Voting in Houses, power of Houses to act notwithstanding vacancies and quorum
excerpt: Decisions are by a majority of members present and voting (the presiding officer votes only on a tie); a House may act despite vacancies; quorum is ten members or one-tenth of the House, whichever is greater.

title: Article 190: Vacation of seats
excerpt: An MLA's or MLC's seat falls vacant on disqualification under Article 191, on resignation, on 60 days' absence without permission, or on holding seats in both Houses; the House may declare the seat vacant.

title: Article 191: Disqualifications for membership
excerpt: Disqualified if the person holds an office of profit, is of unsound mind, is an undischarged insolvent, is not an Indian citizen or has acquired foreign citizenship, or is disqualified under any Parliamentary law (such a

title: Article 192: Decision on questions as to disqualifications of members
excerpt: The Governor decides disqualification questions under Article 191, in accordance with the Election Commission's opinion.

title: Article 193: Penalty for sitting and voting before making oath or affirmation under article 188 or when not qualified or when disqualified
excerpt: An unqualified person who sits or votes in the legislature is liable to a fine of five hundred rupees for each day.

title: Article 194: Powers, privileges, etc., of the Houses of Legislatures and of the members and committees thereof
excerpt: MLAs and MLCs enjoy freedom of speech in the legislature, immunity from court proceedings for votes and speeches, and the House's powers and privileges as defined by the legislature.

title: Article 195: Salaries and allowances of members
excerpt: MLAs' and MLCs' salaries and allowances are fixed by the state legislature by law.

title: Article 196: Provisions as to introduction and passing of Bills
excerpt: A Bill may originate in either House (except Money Bills); it must be passed by the legislature and receive the Governor's assent to become law.

title: Article 197: Restriction on powers of Legislative Council as to Bills other than Money Bills
excerpt: The Council may only delay an ordinary Bill: if the Assembly passes it a second time after three months (one month in the second passage), it is deemed passed by the Council (the Council has at most about four months' de

title: Article 198: Special procedure in respect of Money Bills
excerpt: Money Bills may be introduced only in the Assembly on the Governor's recommendation; the Council has 14 days to recommend amendments, which the Assembly may accept or reject.

title: Article 199: Definition of "Money Bills"
excerpt: A Bill is a Money Bill only if it deals exclusively with taxation, borrowing, the Consolidated or Contingency Funds, appropriation, or audit and accounts; the Speaker's certificate is final.

title: Article 200: Assent to Bills
excerpt: The Governor may assent to a Bill, withhold assent, reserve it for the President's consideration, or return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration; on re-passing, the Governor must assent (the Governor's discretion here is

title: Article 201: Bills reserved for consideration
excerpt: When a Bill is reserved for the President, the President may assent, withhold assent, or direct the Governor to return it for reconsideration within six months; the President is not bound to assent even on re-passing.

title: Article 202: Annual financial statement
excerpt: The Governor causes the Annual Financial Statement (the state budget) to be laid before the legislature each year.

title: Article 203: Procedure in Legislature with respect to estimates
excerpt: Estimates are presented as demands for grants voted by the Assembly; no demand can be made without the Governor's recommendation.

title: Article 204: Appropriation Bills
excerpt: After grants are voted, an Appropriation Bill authorises withdrawal from the state's Consolidated Fund; no amendment varying the amount is allowed.

title: Article 205: Supplementary, additional or excess grants
excerpt: The Governor may lay supplementary, additional or excess demands before the legislature when authorised expenditure proves insufficient.

title: Article 206: Votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants
excerpt: The Assembly may grant a vote on account in advance pending the budget, votes of credit for indefinite demands, and exceptional grants.

title: Article 207: Special provisions as to financial Bills
excerpt: Financial Bills need the Governor's prior recommendation and cannot be introduced in the Legislative Council.

title: Article 208: Rules of procedure
excerpt: Each House of the legislature makes its own rules of procedure and conduct of business.

title: Article 209: Regulation by law of procedure in the Legislature of the State in relation to financial business
excerpt: The state legislature may by law regulate its financial-business procedure to ensure timely completion.

title: Article 210: Language to be used in the Legislature
excerpt: Business is transacted in the state's official language, Hindi or English; English use could be discontinued after 15 years unless continued by the legislature.

title: Article 211: Restriction on discussion in the Legislature
excerpt: No discussion may take place about the conduct of any Supreme Court or High Court judge except on a motion for removal.

title: Article 212: Courts not to inquire into proceedings of the Legislature
excerpt: Courts cannot question the validity of legislative proceedings for alleged irregularity of procedure.

title: Article 213: Power of Governor to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Legislature
excerpt: The Governor may promulgate ordinances when the legislature is not in session if immediate action is needed; an ordinance must be laid before the legislature and lapses six weeks after reassembly.

title: Article 214: High Courts for States
excerpt: There shall be a High Court for each state (one High Court may serve two or more states, such as the common High Court for Punjab and Haryana).

title: Article 215: High Courts to be courts of record
excerpt: Every High Court is a court of record with the power to punish for its own contempt.

title: Article 216: Constitution of High Courts
excerpt: Each High Court consists of a Chief Justice and other judges as the President appoints; judges are appointed by the President under the collegium system.

title: Article 217: Appointment and conditions of the office of a Judge of a High Court
excerpt: High Court judges are appointed by the President; they hold office until age 62 and may be removed only like SC judges (Articles 124(4) and (5)).

title: Article 218: Application of certain provisions relating to Supreme Court to High Courts
excerpt: The provisions on judges' salaries, oath and removal (Articles 124(4) and (5)) apply to High Court judges as well.

title: Article 219: Oath or affirmation by Judges of High Courts
excerpt: A High Court judge takes the oath in the Third Schedule form before the Governor (or a person appointed by the Governor).

title: Article 220: Restriction on practice after being a permanent Judge
excerpt: A permanent High Court judge cannot plead or act in any court or before any authority in India except the Supreme Court and other High Courts.

title: Article 221: Salaries, etc., of Judges
excerpt: High Court judges' salaries and allowances are fixed by Parliament by law and charged on the state's Consolidated Fund; they cannot be varied to a judge's disadvantage.

title: Article 222: Transfer of a Judge from one High Court to another
excerpt: The President may, after consulting the Chief Justice of India, transfer a High Court judge to another High Court (judicial review of transfers was recognised in the First Judges case).

title: Article 223: Appointment of acting Chief Justice
excerpt: When the Chief Justice's office is vacant or the CJ is absent or unable to perform duties, the President appoints another judge as acting Chief Justice.

title: Article 224: Appointment of additional and acting Judges
excerpt: The President may appoint additional judges for temporary workload increases (up to two years) and acting judges during a permanent judge's absence.

title: Article 224A: Appointment of retired Judges at sittings of High Courts
excerpt: The Chief Justice of a High Court, with the President's prior consent, may request a retired High Court judge to sit and act as a judge (42nd Amendment 1976).

title: Article 225: Jurisdiction of existing High Courts
excerpt: The existing High Courts' jurisdiction and the laws on their powers continue, subject to the Constitution and laws made by the appropriate legislature.

title: Article 226: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
excerpt: Every High Court may issue writs (habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, certiorari) for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose; wider than the Supreme Court's Article 32 power.

title: Article 227: Power of superintendence over all courts by the High Court
excerpt: Every High Court has superintendence over all courts and tribunals in its territory (except military tribunals), including calling for returns and making rules of practice.

title: Article 228: Transfer of certain cases to High Court
excerpt: A High Court may withdraw to itself a case involving a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution pending in a subordinate court.

title: Article 229: Officers and servants and the expenses of High Courts
excerpt: The Chief Justice appoints the High Court's officers and servants; administrative expenses are charged on the state's Consolidated Fund.

title: Article 230: Extension of jurisdiction of High Courts to Union territories
excerpt: Parliament may by law extend or exclude a High Court's jurisdiction to or from a Union Territory.

title: Article 231: Establishment of a common High Court for two or more States
excerpt: Parliament may by law establish a common High Court for two or more states or for states and a Union Territory (e.g. the former common High Court for the north-eastern states).

title: Article 232: Interpretation
excerpt: Was an interpretation clause for this Chapter; omitted by the 7th Amendment 1956 when the Part B states were reorganised.

title: Article 233: Appointment of district judges
excerpt: District judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court; a person not already in judicial service must have seven years' Bar practice and be recommended by the High Court.

title: Article 233A: Validation of appointments of, and judgments, etc., delivered by, certain district judges
excerpt: Validates certain district judge appointments, postings and judgments made before the 20th Amendment 1966 that would otherwise be invalid for procedural defects.

title: Article 234: Recruitment of persons other than district judges to the judicial service
excerpt: Judicial service appointments below district judge are made by the Governor under rules framed after consulting the State Public Service Commission and the High Court.

title: Article 235: Control over subordinate courts
excerpt: Control over district and subordinate courts, including postings, promotions and leave, vests in the High Court.

title: Article 236: Interpretation
excerpt: Defines 'district judge' and 'judicial service' for this Chapter.

title: Article 237: Application of the provisions of this Chapter to certain class or classes of magistrates
excerpt: The Governor may by public notification apply the subordinate-courts provisions to any class of magistrates in the state, as if references to district judges included those magistrates.

title: Article 238: Application of provisions of Part VI to States in Part B of the First Schedule
excerpt: Applied Part VI to the former Part B states; became redundant and was omitted by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 239: Administration of Union territories
excerpt: Union Territories are administered by the President acting through an Administrator (Lieutenant Governor); the President may also appoint a state's Governor as a UT's Administrator.

title: Article 239AA: Special provisions with respect to Delhi
excerpt: Gives the National Capital Territory of Delhi a Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers with power over State and Concurrent List subjects except public order, police and land; inserted by the 69th Amendment 1991 a

title: Article 239AB: Provision in case of failure of constitutional machinery
excerpt: If Delhi's administration cannot be carried on per Article 239AA, the President may suspend provisions of Article 239AA on the Administrator's report (69th Amendment 1991).

title: Article 239B: Power of administrator to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Legislature
excerpt: A UT Administrator may promulgate ordinances when the UT legislature is not in session, with the President's prior instructions; an ordinance lapses six weeks after the legislature reassembles.

title: Article 240: Power of Parliament to make laws for certain Union territories
excerpt: Parliament may make laws for Union Territories without legislatures on any subject, and the President may make regulations for certain UTs (Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and D

title: Article 241: High Courts for Union territories
excerpt: Parliament may by law constitute a High Court for a Union Territory or extend an existing High Court's jurisdiction to it.

title: Article 242: Coorg
excerpt: Dealt with the Part C state of Coorg; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956 when Coorg merged into Mysore state.

title: Article 243: Definitions
excerpt: Defines 'district', 'Gram Sabha', 'intermediate level', 'Panchayat', 'Panchayat area' and 'village' for this Part (73rd Amendment 1992).

title: Article 243A: Gram Sabha
excerpt: A Gram Sabha (all voters of a village) may exercise powers and perform functions at village level as the state legislature provides by law.

title: Article 243B: Constitution of Panchayats
excerpt: There shall be Panchayats at village, intermediate and district levels in every state (intermediate level may be skipped in states below 20 lakh population).

title: Article 243C: Composition of Panchayats
excerpt: All Panchayat seats are filled by direct election; the chairperson at intermediate and district levels is elected indirectly; MLAs and MPs may be represented as the state legislature provides.

title: Article 243D: Reservation of seats
excerpt: Seats are reserved for SCs and STs in proportion to population, with at least one-third reserved for women (including within SC/ST quotas); states may also reserve seats for backward classes.

title: Article 243E: Duration of Panchayats, etc.
excerpt: A Panchayat's term is five years; elections must be completed before its term expires; a dissolved Panchayat's fresh election must be held within six months, and the new body serves only the remainder of the term.

title: Article 243F: Disqualifications for membership
excerpt: A person is disqualified from Panchayat membership if disqualified under any law for the state legislature's election, or under any state law; minimum age 21.

title: Article 243G: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats
excerpt: State legislatures may endow Panchayats with powers to function as institutions of self-government, including preparing plans for economic development and social justice and implementing schemes in the Eleventh Schedule'

title: Article 243H: Powers to impose taxes by, and Funds of, the Panchayats
excerpt: State legislatures may authorise Panchayats to levy and collect taxes, assign state revenues to them, and provide for grants-in-aid and Panchayat Funds.

title: Article 243-I: Constitution of Finance Commission to review financial position
excerpt: The Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every five years to review Panchayats' finances and recommend principles for distributing state revenues to them.

title: Article 243J: Audit of accounts of Panchayats
excerpt: State legislatures may provide for maintenance and audit of Panchayat accounts.

title: Article 243K: Elections to the Panchayats
excerpt: Panchayat elections are conducted under the superintendence, direction and control of the State Election Commission.

title: Article 243L: Application to Union territories
excerpt: This Part applies to Union Territories, with the President empowered to direct exceptions and modifications; Delhi is exempted.

title: Article 243M: Part not to apply to certain areas
excerpt: This Part does not apply to Scheduled Areas and tribal areas in certain north-eastern states, nor to specified hill areas of Manipur; Parliament may extend Panchayat provisions to Scheduled Areas (done by PESA, 1996).

title: Article 243N: Continuance of existing laws and Panchayats
excerpt: Pre-73rd Amendment Panchayat laws continue for one year unless repealed; existing Panchayats continued till their term's end.

title: Article 243O: Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters
excerpt: Courts cannot question Panchayat elections except by an election petition presented as the state legislature provides.

title: Article 243P: Definitions
excerpt: Defines 'Committee', 'district', 'Metropolitan area', 'Municipal area', 'Municipality', 'panchayat' and 'population' for this Part (74th Amendment 1992).

title: Article 243Q: Constitution of Municipalities
excerpt: There shall be a Nagar Panchayat for transitional areas, a Municipal Council for smaller urban areas, and a Municipal Corporation for larger urban areas in every state.

title: Article 243R: Composition of Municipalities
excerpt: All municipal seats are filled by direct election; the chairperson is elected as the state legislature provides; persons with special knowledge may be represented without voting rights.

title: Article 243S: Constitution and composition of Wards Committees, etc.
excerpt: Wards Committees are constituted for municipalities with 3 lakh or more population, with members chosen from the ward's elected councillors.

title: Article 243T: Reservation of seats
excerpt: Seats are reserved for SCs and STs in proportion to population, with at least one-third reserved for women (including within SC/ST quotas).

title: Article 243U: Duration of Municipalities, etc.
excerpt: A municipality's term is five years; elections must precede its expiry; a dissolved municipality's fresh election must be held within six months, serving only the remainder of the term.

title: Article 243V: Disqualifications for membership
excerpt: A person is disqualified from municipal membership if disqualified under any law for the state legislature's election, or under any state law; minimum age 21.

title: Article 243W: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities, etc.
excerpt: State legislatures may endow municipalities with powers to function as institutions of self-government, including plans for economic development and social justice and schemes in the Twelfth Schedule's 18 subjects.

title: Article 243X: Power to impose taxes by, and Funds of, the Municipalities
excerpt: State legislatures may authorise municipalities to levy and collect taxes, assign state revenues, and provide for grants-in-aid and Municipal Funds.

title: Article 243Y: Finance Commission
excerpt: The State Finance Commission constituted under Article 243-I also reviews municipalities' finances and recommends revenue distribution.

title: Article 243Z: Audit of accounts of Municipalities
excerpt: State legislatures may provide for maintenance and audit of municipal accounts.

title: Article 243ZA: Elections to the Municipalities
excerpt: Municipal elections are conducted under the superintendence, direction and control of the State Election Commission.

title: Article 243ZB: Application to Union territories
excerpt: This Part applies to Union Territories, with the President empowered to direct exceptions and modifications.

title: Article 243ZC: Part not to apply to certain areas
excerpt: This Part does not apply to Scheduled Areas and tribal areas under Article 244(1) and (2).

title: Article 243ZD: Committee for district planning
excerpt: A District Planning Committee consolidates plans prepared by Panchayats and municipalities in each district.

title: Article 243ZE: Committee for Metropolitan planning
excerpt: A Metropolitan Planning Committee prepares draft development plans for each metropolitan area (population of 10 lakh or more).

title: Article 243ZF: Continuance of existing laws and Municipalities
excerpt: Pre-74th Amendment municipal laws continue for one year unless repealed; existing municipalities continued till their term's end.

title: Article 243ZG: Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters
excerpt: Courts cannot question municipal elections except by an election petition presented as the state legislature provides.

title: Article 243ZH: Definitions
excerpt: Defines 'authorised person', 'board', 'co-operative society', 'multi-State co-operative society', 'officer', 'Registrar', 'State Act' and 'State level co-operative society' for this Part (97th Amendment 2011).

title: Article 243ZI: Incorporation of co-operative societies
excerpt: State legislatures make laws for incorporation, regulation and winding up of co-operative societies based on voluntary formation, democratic member-control and professional management. Note: in Rajendra Shah (2013) the S

title: Article 243ZJ: Number and term of members of board and its office bearers
excerpt: A co-operative society's board has up to 21 directors with a five-year term; co-opted members and functional directors are provided for.

title: Article 243ZK: Election of members of board
excerpt: Board elections are conducted before the term's expiry under the superintendence of an authority designated by the state government.

title: Article 243ZL: Supersession and suspension of board and interim management
excerpt: A board may be superseded or kept under suspension only in specified situations (persistent default, negligence, etc.) and for a limited period.

title: Article 243ZM: Audit of accounts of co-operative societies
excerpt: Co-operative societies must get their accounts audited by auditors from a state-approved panel; audit reports go to the general body.

title: Article 243ZN: Convening of general body meetings
excerpt: The society's annual general body meeting must be convened within six months of the financial year's close.

title: Article 243ZO: Right of a member to get information
excerpt: Members have the right to access the society's books, information and accounts relating to transactions with them.

title: Article 243ZP: Returns
excerpt: Every co-operative society files annual returns to the Registrar within six months of the financial year's close.

title: Article 243ZQ: Offences and penalties
excerpt: State legislatures prescribe offences and penalties relating to co-operative societies (false returns, disobedience of Registrar's orders, etc.).

title: Article 243ZR: Application to multi-State co-operative societies
excerpt: This Part applies to multi-State co-operative societies with Parliament as the competent legislature (upheld for multi-state societies in the Supreme Court's 2021 ruling).

title: Article 243ZS: Application to Union territories
excerpt: This Part applies to Union Territories with the President empowered to direct exceptions and modifications.

title: Article 243ZT: Continuance of existing laws
excerpt: Pre-97th Amendment co-operative society laws continue for one year unless repealed or amended.

title: Article 244: Administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas
excerpt: Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are administered under the Fifth Schedule; the tribal areas of those four states under the Sixth Schedule.

title: Article 244A: Formation of an autonomous State comprising certain tribal areas in Assam and creation of local Legislature or Council of Ministers or both therefor
excerpt: Parliament may by law form an autonomous state within Assam comprising specified tribal areas, with its own legislature or Council of Ministers (22nd Amendment 1969; used for Meghalaya's creation).

title: Article 245: Extent of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States
excerpt: Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of India; a state legislature only for its state (or part of it); no Parliamentary law is invalid merely for extra-territorial operation.

title: Article 246: Subject-matter of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States
excerpt: Distributes legislative subjects via the Seventh Schedule: Parliament over the Union List, states over the State List, both over the Concurrent List; Parliament alone over residuary subjects (Entry 97, Union List).

title: Article 246A: Special provision with respect to goods and services tax
excerpt: Both Parliament and state legislatures may make laws on GST: Parliament on inter-state supply (IGST) and states on intra-state supply (SGST/CGST); inserted by the 101st Amendment 2016.

title: Article 247: Power of Parliament to provide for the establishment of certain additional courts
excerpt: Parliament may establish additional courts for better administration of its laws and matters in the Union List.

title: Article 248: Residuary powers of legislation
excerpt: Parliament has exclusive power over subjects not enumerated in the State or Concurrent Lists, including taxes not mentioned in either list.

title: Article 249: Power of Parliament to legislate with respect to a matter in the State List in the national interest
excerpt: Parliament may legislate on a State List subject if the Rajya Sabha resolves by two-thirds of members present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest; the resolution lasts one year, renewable.

title: Article 250: Power of Parliament to legislate with respect to any matter in the State List if a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation
excerpt: During a National Emergency, Parliament may legislate on any State List subject; such laws cease six months after the Emergency ends.

title: Article 251: Inconsistency between laws made by Parliament under articles 249 and 250 and laws made by the Legislatures of States
excerpt: A state law repugnant to a Parliamentary law made under Articles 249 or 250 prevails only so long as the Parliamentary law is in force.

title: Article 252: Power of Parliament to legislate for two or more States by consent and adoption of such legislation by any other State
excerpt: If two or more states' legislatures resolve that Parliament should regulate a State List matter, Parliament may do so and other states may adopt it (used for the Urban Land Ceiling Act, 1976).

title: Article 253: Legislation for giving effect to international agreements
excerpt: Parliament may make laws for implementing treaties and international agreements even on State List subjects (the basis of environmental and trade legislation).

title: Article 254: Inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and laws made by the Legislatures of States
excerpt: On Concurrent List subjects, a Parliamentary law prevails over a repugnant state law; a state law reserved for and assented to by the President prevails in that state unless Parliament later overrides it (the doctrine of

title: Article 255: Requirements as to recommendations and previous sanctions to be regarded as matters of procedure only
excerpt: Want of prior recommendation or sanction is a procedural matter: an Act is not invalid merely because assent was given without it, unless the provision itself required it.

title: Article 256: Obligation of States and the Union
excerpt: State executive power must ensure compliance with Parliamentary laws; the Union's executive power extends to giving directions to states for that purpose.

title: Article 257: Control of the Union over States in certain cases
excerpt: The Union may give directions to states on the construction and maintenance of means of communication of national or military importance and on protection of railways; the extra cost is borne by the Union.

title: Article 257A: Assistance to States by deployment of armed forces or other forces of the Union
excerpt: Let the Union deploy armed or other forces in a state to deal with a grave law-and-order situation; inserted by the 42nd Amendment 1976 and repealed by the 44th Amendment 1978.

title: Article 258: Power of the Union to confer powers, etc., on States in certain cases
excerpt: The President, with a state's Governor's consent, may entrust Union executive functions to the state government or its officers.

title: Article 258A: Power of the States to entrust functions to the Union
excerpt: A state's Governor, with the President's consent, may entrust state executive functions to the Union government or its officers (42nd Amendment 1976).

title: Article 259: Armed Forces in States in Part B of the First Schedule
excerpt: Dealt with armed forces in Part B states; omitted by the 7th Amendment 1956.
