title: Article 260: Jurisdiction of the Union in relation to territories outside India
excerpt: The Union government may exercise jurisdiction in foreign territory by treaty, agreement, grant, usage, sufferance or other lawful means.

title: Article 261: Public acts, records and judicial proceedings
excerpt: Full faith and credit is given throughout India to public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every state; Parliament regulates their proof and effect.

title: Article 262: Adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers or river valleys
excerpt: Parliament may provide for adjudication of inter-state river water disputes (Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956); Parliament may also bar the Supreme Court and other courts from such disputes (used for tribunals

title: Article 263: Provisions with respect to an inter-State Council
excerpt: The President may establish an Inter-State Council to inquire into and advise on inter-state disputes and subjects of common interest; the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation led to its creation in 1990.

title: Article 264: Interpretation
excerpt: Defines 'Finance Commission' for this Part.

title: Article 265: Taxes not to be imposed save by authority of law
excerpt: No tax can be levied or collected except by authority of law (the constitutional basis for challenging illegal taxation).

title: Article 266: Consolidated Funds and public accounts of India and of the States
excerpt: All revenues form the Consolidated Fund of India (or of the state); money is paid out only under appropriation by law; other public moneys go to the Public Account.

title: Article 267: Contingency Fund
excerpt: Parliament (and state legislatures) may establish a Contingency Fund in the nature of an imprest, placed at the President's (or Governor's) disposal for unforeseen expenditure.

title: Article 268: Duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States
excerpt: Stamp duties and excise duties on medicinal and toilet preparations are levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the states where levied.

title: Article 268A: Service tax levied by Union and collected and appropriated by the Union and the States
excerpt: Gave the Union power over service tax with collection shared with states; omitted by the 101st Amendment 2016 when GST replaced service tax.

title: Article 269: Taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States
excerpt: Taxes on sale or purchase of goods (other than newspapers) and taxes on consignment of goods in inter-state trade are levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the states.

title: Article 269A: Levy and collection of goods and services tax in course of inter-State trade or commerce
excerpt: IGST on inter-state supply is levied and collected by the Union and apportioned between the Union and states on GST Council recommendations (101st Amendment 2016).

title: Article 270: Taxes levied and distributed between the Union and the States
excerpt: All Union taxes and duties (except specified exclusions) form the divisible pool shared with states on Finance Commission recommendations; states currently receive 41 percent under the 15th Finance Commission.

title: Article 271: Surcharge on certain duties and taxes for purposes of the Union
excerpt: Parliament may levy a surcharge on Union duties and taxes (except GST) for Union purposes; surcharge proceeds go wholly to the Union.

title: Article 272: Taxes which are levied and collected by the Union and may be distributed between the Union and the States
excerpt: Covered Union excise duties shareable with states; omitted by the 101st Amendment 2016 in the GST overhaul.

title: Article 273: Grants in lieu of export duty on jute and jute products
excerpt: Provides for grants-in-aid to Assam, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal in lieu of the former jute export duty.

title: Article 274: Prior recommendation of President required to Bills affecting taxation in which States are interested
excerpt: Bills affecting taxation in which states are interested need the President's prior recommendation.

title: Article 275: Grants from the Union to certain States
excerpt: Parliament may provide grants-in-aid to states in need of assistance, charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; includes grants for tribal welfare and raising administration in Scheduled Areas.

title: Article 276: Taxes on professions, trades, callings and employments
excerpt: States (and local bodies) may levy professional tax up to the prescribed ceiling, currently 2,500 rupees per person per year.

title: Article 277: Savings
excerpt: Taxes, duties, cesses or fees lawfully levied by states or local bodies before the Constitution's commencement continue until Parliament provides otherwise.

title: Article 278: Agreement with States in Part B of the First Schedule with regard to certain financial matters
excerpt: Dealt with financial agreements with Part B states; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 279: Calculation of "net proceeds", etc.
excerpt: Defines how net proceeds of taxes and duties are calculated (gross proceeds minus cost of collection), certified by the CAG whose certificate is final.

title: Article 279A: Goods and Services Tax Council
excerpt: Constitutes the GST Council (Union Finance Minister as chair, state finance ministers as members) to recommend GST rates, exemptions and thresholds; decisions need a three-fourths majority with the Union holding one-thir

title: Article 280: Finance Commission
excerpt: The President constitutes a Finance Commission every five years (or earlier) to recommend the distribution of tax proceeds between the Union and states and among states, and grants-in-aid; the 16th Finance Commission (Ar

title: Article 281: Recommendations of the Finance Commission
excerpt: The President lays the Finance Commission's recommendations and the action-taken memorandum before each House of Parliament.

title: Article 282: Expenditure defrayable by the Union or a State out of its revenues
excerpt: The Union or a state may make grants for any public purpose even beyond its legislative competence (used for centrally sponsored schemes).

title: Article 283: Custody, etc., of Consolidated Funds, Contingency Funds and moneys credited to the public accounts
excerpt: The custody and payment of moneys into and out of these funds is regulated by Parliamentary (or state) law, and by Presidential (or gubernatorial) rules until then.

title: Article 284: Custody of suitors' deposits and other moneys received by public servants and courts
excerpt: Moneys received by public servants or courts (other than revenues) are paid into the Public Account of India or the state.

title: Article 285: Exemption of property of the Union from State taxation
excerpt: Union property is exempt from state taxation unless Parliament provides otherwise.

title: Article 286: Restrictions as to imposition of tax on the sale or purchase of goods
excerpt: Restricts states' power to tax sale or purchase of goods outside the state or in inter-state trade or commerce (scope reshaped by the 101st Amendment's GST provisions).

title: Article 287: Exemption from taxes on electricity
excerpt: States cannot tax electricity consumed by the Union or sold to it for its consumption, except under pre-Constitution laws or with the President's assent.

title: Article 288: Exemption from taxation by States in respect of water or electricity in certain cases
excerpt: States cannot tax water or electricity stored, generated or carried by an inter-state river authority without the President's prior sanction.

title: Article 289: Exemption of property and income of a State from Union taxation
excerpt: State property and income are exempt from Union taxation; Parliament may tax state business operations by law.

title: Article 290: Adjustment in respect of certain expenses and pensions
excerpt: The Union and states adjust between themselves expenses and pensions relating to transferred functions and pre-Constitution liabilities.

title: Article 290A: Annual payment to certain Devaswom Funds
excerpt: Kerala pays 46.5 lakh rupees annually to the Travancore Devaswom Fund and 13.5 lakh rupees to the Cochin Devaswom Fund, charged on the state's Consolidated Fund (7th Amendment 1956).

title: Article 291: Privy purse sums of Rulers
excerpt: Guaranteed privy purse payments to former rulers; repealed by the 26th Amendment 1971 which abolished privy purses.

title: Article 292: Borrowing by the Government of India
excerpt: The Union government may borrow on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India within limits fixed by Parliament.

title: Article 293: Borrowing by States
excerpt: States may borrow on their Consolidated Fund's security within limits fixed by the legislature; a state indebted to the Union needs the Union's consent to borrow further.

title: Article 294: Succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations in certain cases
excerpt: Union and state governments succeed to the property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations of the Dominion of India and corresponding provinces.

title: Article 295: Succession to property, assets, rights, liabilities and obligations in other cases
excerpt: Property and assets that vested in His Majesty for the Dominion or a province vest in the Union or the corresponding state, with liabilities apportioned.

title: Article 296: Property accruing by escheat or lapse or as bona vacantia
excerpt: Property accruing by escheat, lapse or as bona vacantia (ownerless property) vests in the state where situated, or in the Union otherwise.

title: Article 297: Things of value within territorial waters or continental shelf and resources of the exclusive economic zone to vest in the Union
excerpt: All lands, minerals and other things of value in territorial waters, the continental shelf and the exclusive economic zone vest in the Union (basis of offshore oil and mineral rights).

title: Article 298: Power to carry on trade or business
excerpt: The Union and states may carry on any trade or business, acquire and dispose of property, and make contracts for any purpose.

title: Article 299: Contracts
excerpt: Government contracts must be expressed to be made by the President (or Governor), executed by authorised persons, and cannot make the President or Governor personally liable.

title: Article 300: Suits and proceedings
excerpt: The Government of India may sue or be sued as the Union of India, and a state government as the state, in matters arising from this Part's succession and contract provisions.

title: Article 300A: Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law
excerpt: No person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law; inserted by the 44th Amendment 1978, making property a constitutional legal right rather than a fundamental right.

title: Article 301: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse
excerpt: Trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India shall be free, subject to the other provisions of this Part (basis of the common-market doctrine in Atiabari and Automobile Transport cases).

title: Article 302: Power of Parliament to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse
excerpt: Parliament may restrict trade freedom in the public interest.

title: Article 303: Restrictions on the legislative powers of the Union and of the States with regard to trade and commerce
excerpt: Neither Parliament nor state legislatures may prefer one state over another or discriminate between states in trade and commerce laws, except to deal with scarcity of goods.

title: Article 304: Restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse among States
excerpt: States may impose reasonable restrictions in the public interest and non-discriminatory taxes on imported goods, but Bills for the former need the President's prior sanction.

title: Article 305: Saving of existing laws and laws providing for State monopolies
excerpt: Existing laws and laws creating state monopolies are saved from Articles 301 and 303 (amended by the 4th Amendment 1955).

title: Article 306: Power of certain States in Part B of the First Schedule to impose restrictions on trade and commerce
excerpt: Let Part B states impose trade restrictions; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956 and not in force.

title: Article 307: Appointment of authority for carrying out the purposes of articles 301 to 304
excerpt: Parliament may appoint an authority to carry out the purposes of Articles 301 to 304 and confer on it necessary powers (no such authority has been appointed).

title: Article 308: Interpretation
excerpt: Defines 'State' for this Part as including Union Territories (with adaptations for J and K, which no longer applies after the 2019 reorganisation).

title: Article 309: Recruitment and conditions of service of persons serving the Union or a State
excerpt: Parliament (for Union services) and state legislatures (for state services) regulate recruitment and service conditions; until then the President or Governor regulates them by rules.

title: Article 310: Tenure of office of persons serving the Union or a State
excerpt: Civil servants hold office during the President's or Governor's pleasure, except as expressly provided by the Constitution.

title: Article 311: Dismissal, removal or reduction in rank of persons employed in civil capacities under the Union or a State
excerpt: A civil servant cannot be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to the appointing authority, and cannot be dismissed without an inquiry with a reasonable opportunity of being heard (the Article 311(2) safeguar

title: Article 312: All-India services
excerpt: If the Rajya Sabha resolves by two-thirds of members present and voting, Parliament may create new All-India Services (IAS, IPS and IFS exist under this Article; the 28th Amendment 1972 extended it to the All-India Judic

title: Article 312A: Power of Parliament to vary or revoke conditions of service of officers of certain services
excerpt: Empowers Parliament to vary or revoke pre-Constitution service conditions of ICS and other officers (28th Amendment 1972).

title: Article 313: Transitional provisions
excerpt: Pre-Constitution laws on public services continue until replaced under Article 309.

title: Article 314: Provision for protection of existing officers of certain services
excerpt: Protected ICS and other pre-Constitution officers' service conditions; repealed by the 28th Amendment 1972.

title: Article 315: Public Service Commissions for the Union and for the States
excerpt: There shall be a Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and a Public Service Commission for each state.

title: Article 316: Appointment and term of office of members
excerpt: The UPSC Chairman and members are appointed by the President, and state PSC members by the Governor; they hold office for six years or until age 65 (UPSC) or 62 (state PSC).

title: Article 317: Removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission
excerpt: A PSC member can be removed only by the President on the Supreme Court's report after inquiry, on grounds of misbehaviour; the President may suspend a member pending inquiry.

title: Article 318: Power to make regulations as to conditions of service of members and staff of the Commission
excerpt: The President (for UPSC) or Governor (for state PSCs) makes regulations on the number of members, their service conditions and staff.

title: Article 319: Prohibition as to the holding of offices by members of Commission on ceasing to be such members
excerpt: A UPSC Chairman cannot take further government employment; other members face restrictions on future offices to protect the Commission's independence.

title: Article 320: Functions of Public Service Commissions
excerpt: PSCs conduct examinations for appointments, advise on recruitment methods, promotions, transfers and disciplinary matters; consultation with the PSC is required on specified matters.

title: Article 321: Power to extend functions of Public Service Commissions
excerpt: Parliament or a state legislature may extend a PSC's functions by law.

title: Article 322: Expenses of Public Service Commissions
excerpt: UPSC expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; state PSC expenses on the state's Consolidated Fund.

title: Article 323: Reports of Public Service Commissions
excerpt: The UPSC reports annually to the President and state PSCs to the Governor, who lay the reports with action-taken memoranda before the legislature.

title: Article 323A: Administrative tribunals
excerpt: Parliament may establish administrative tribunals for service disputes of Union, state and local government employees (42nd Amendment 1976; the Central Administrative Tribunal was set up under the Administrative Tribunal

title: Article 323B: Tribunals for other matters
excerpt: The appropriate legislature may establish tribunals for tax, industrial, land reform, election and other specified disputes (42nd Amendment 1976; tribunal powers were limited by L. Chandra Kumar, 1997).

title: Article 324: Superintendence, direction and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission
excerpt: Elections to Parliament, state legislatures, the President and Vice-President are supervised by the Election Commission, headed by the Chief Election Commissioner and other Commissioners (appointed under the CEC Act, 202

title: Article 325: No person to be ineligible for inclusion in, or to claim to be included in a special, electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex
excerpt: One general electoral roll per constituency; no one may be excluded or included in a separate roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.

title: Article 326: Elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of States to be on the basis of adult suffrage
excerpt: Elections are on the basis of adult suffrage: every Indian citizen aged 18 or above may vote (voting age lowered from 21 by the 61st Amendment 1988).

title: Article 327: Power of Parliament to make provision with respect to elections to Legislatures
excerpt: Parliament may make laws on all electoral matters for Parliament and state legislatures (Representation of the People Acts, 1950 and 1951).

title: Article 328: Power of Legislature of a State to make provision with respect to elections to such Legislature
excerpt: A state legislature may make electoral laws for its own House, subject to Parliamentary law.

title: Article 329: Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters
excerpt: The validity of laws on delimitation and seat allotment cannot be questioned in court; elections can be challenged only by an election petition (Article 329(b)).

title: Article 329A: Special provision as to elections to Parliament in the case of Prime Minister and Speaker
excerpt: Shielded the elections of the PM and Speaker from court challenge; inserted by the 39th Amendment 1975 during the Emergency and repealed by the 44th Amendment 1978.

title: Article 330: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the House of the People
excerpt: Seats are reserved in the Lok Sabha for SCs and STs in proportion to their population in each state.

title: Article 331: Representation of the Anglo-Indian community in the House of the People
excerpt: Let the President nominate up to two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha if the community was under-represented; omitted by the 104th Amendment 2019 with effect from 25 January 2020.

title: Article 332: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Legislative Assemblies of the States
excerpt: Seats are reserved in state Assemblies for SCs and STs in proportion to their population.

title: Article 333: Representation of the Anglo-Indian community in the Legislative Assemblies of the States
excerpt: Let Governors nominate Anglo-Indians to state Assemblies; omitted by the 104th Amendment 2019.

title: Article 334: Reservation of seats and special representation to cease after certain period
excerpt: The SC/ST reservation provisions (Articles 330 and 332) were originally to cease after ten years but have been extended repeatedly; the 104th Amendment 2019 extended them to 25 January 2030.

title: Article 335: Claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to services and posts
excerpt: SC/ST claims are considered in appointments to Union and state services consistently with maintaining administrative efficiency.

title: Article 336: Special provision for Anglo-Indian community in certain services
excerpt: Reserved Anglo-Indian quotas in railway, customs, postal and telegraph services for the first two years, extended to ten years; long expired.

title: Article 337: Special provision with respect to educational grants for the benefit of Anglo-Indian community
excerpt: Protected Anglo-Indian educational grants for the first three financial years, extendable by ten years; long expired.

title: Article 338: National Commission for Scheduled Castes
excerpt: Constitutes the National Commission for Scheduled Castes to investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints and advise on SC welfare (separated from the combined SC/ST Commission by the 89th Amendment 2003).

title: Article 338A: National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
excerpt: Constitutes the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes to investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints and advise on ST welfare (89th Amendment 2003).

title: Article 338B: National Commission for Backward Classes
excerpt: Gives constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (102nd Amendment 2018), which investigates and monitors safeguards for socially and educationally backward classes.

title: Article 339: Control of the Union over the administration of Scheduled Areas and the welfare of Scheduled Tribes
excerpt: The President may direct states on drawing up and executing tribal welfare schemes; a Commission reports on Scheduled Areas and ST administration (the Dhebar Commission was appointed under this Article).

title: Article 340: Appointment of a Commission to investigate the conditions of backward classes
excerpt: The President may appoint a Commission to investigate backward-class conditions and recommend steps (the Kalelkar Commission 1953 and Mandal Commission 1979 were appointed under this Article).

title: Article 341: Scheduled Castes
excerpt: The President, after consulting a state's Governor, notifies the castes deemed Scheduled Castes for that state; Parliament alone may include or exclude castes by law.

title: Article 342: Scheduled Tribes
excerpt: The President, after consulting a state's Governor, notifies the tribes deemed Scheduled Tribes; Parliament alone may include or exclude tribes by law.

title: Article 342A: Socially and educationally backward classes
excerpt: The President notifies the socially and educationally backward classes for each state or Union Territory in consultation with the Governor; Parliament alone may amend the list; states keep power to identify SEBCs for the

title: Article 343: Official language of the Union
excerpt: Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language of the Union; the international form of Indian numerals is used for official purposes.

title: Article 344: Commission and Committee of Parliament on official language
excerpt: The President constitutes an Official Language Commission every five years and a Parliamentary Committee examines its recommendations (the first Commission was appointed in 1955).

title: Article 345: Official language or languages of a State
excerpt: A state legislature may adopt any language in use in the state (or Hindi) as its official language.

title: Article 346: Official language for communication between one State and another or between a State and the Union
excerpt: The Union's official language is used for inter-state and Union-state communication, unless states agree on Hindi between themselves.

title: Article 347: Special provision relating to language spoken by a section of the population of a State
excerpt: The President may recognise a language spoken by a substantial section of a state's population for official purposes on their demand.

title: Article 348: Language to be used in the Supreme Court and in the High Courts and for Acts, Bills, etc.
excerpt: English is used for Supreme Court and High Court proceedings and for authoritative texts of Bills, Acts and orders, until Parliament provides otherwise.

title: Article 349: Special procedure for enactment of certain laws relating to language
excerpt: Bills on the language of courts and laws need the President's prior sanction and consideration of the Language Commission's recommendations during the first fifteen years.

title: Article 350: Language to be used in representations for redress of grievances
excerpt: Every person may submit representations for redress of grievances to Union or state authorities in any language used in the Union or the state.

title: Article 350A: Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage
excerpt: States and local authorities must provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to linguistic minority children (7th Amendment 1956).

title: Article 350B: Special Officer for linguistic minorities
excerpt: The President appoints a Special Officer (Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities) to investigate safeguards for linguistic minorities and report to the President (7th Amendment 1956).

title: Article 351: Directive for development of the Hindi language
excerpt: It is the Union's duty to promote the spread of Hindi and develop it as a medium of expression of India's composite culture, drawing on Sanskrit and other Indian languages.

title: Article 352: Proclamation of Emergency
excerpt: The President may proclaim a National Emergency on the ground of war, external aggression or armed rebellion (substituted for 'internal disturbance' by the 44th Amendment 1978), only on the written advice of the Cabinet;

title: Article 353: Effect of Proclamation of Emergency
excerpt: During a National Emergency the Union's executive power extends to giving directions to states, and Parliament may legislate on State List subjects.

title: Article 354: Application of provisions relating to distribution of revenues while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation
excerpt: The President may modify the revenue-distribution provisions (Articles 268 to 279) during a National Emergency.

title: Article 355: Duty of the Union to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance
excerpt: The Union must protect every state against external aggression and internal disturbance and ensure state governments run per the Constitution (invoked for central intervention debates).

title: Article 356: Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in States
excerpt: The President may impose President's Rule in a state on the Governor's report (or otherwise) if its government cannot run per the Constitution; it needs Parliamentary approval within two months and can last up to three y

title: Article 357: Exercise of legislative powers under Proclamation issued under article 356
excerpt: Parliament may confer the state legislature's law-making power on the President during President's Rule, and authorise expenditure from the state's Consolidated Fund.

title: Article 358: Suspension of provisions of article 19 during emergencies
excerpt: Article 19 freedoms are automatically suspended during a National Emergency on war or external aggression (not on armed rebellion); the 44th Amendment confined this to war and external aggression only.

title: Article 359: Suspension of the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III during emergencies
excerpt: The President may suspend the right to move courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights (except Articles 20 and 21, which the 44th Amendment made non-suspendable) during an Emergency.

title: Article 360: Provisions as to financial emergency
excerpt: The President may proclaim a Financial Emergency if India's financial stability or credit is threatened; it needs Parliamentary approval within two months; Union directions may include salary reductions of government ser

title: Article 361: Protection of President and Governors and Rajpramukhs
excerpt: The President and Governors are not answerable to any court for acts done in the exercise of their powers; no criminal proceedings can be instituted against them during their term.

title: Article 361A: Protection of publication of proceedings of Parliament and State Legislatures
excerpt: Protects publication of substantially true reports of Parliamentary and legislature proceedings (44th Amendment 1978; the Feroze Gandhi Act's constitutional basis).

title: Article 361B: Disqualification for appointment on remunerative political post
excerpt: A legislator disqualified under the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection) cannot hold a remunerative political post until re-elected or five years pass, whichever is earlier (91st Amendment 2003).

title: Article 362: Rights and privileges of Rulers of Indian States
excerpt: Guaranteed the rights and privileges of former rulers; repealed by the 26th Amendment 1971.

title: Article 363: Bar to interference by courts in disputes arising out of certain treaties, agreements, etc.
excerpt: Courts cannot decide disputes arising from pre-Constitution treaties, covenants and sanads of former rulers (used in privy purse litigation).

title: Article 363A: Recognition granted to Rulers of Indian States to cease and privy purses to be abolished
excerpt: Ended recognition of former rulers and abolished privy purses (26th Amendment 1971).

title: Article 364: Special provisions as to major ports and aerodromes
excerpt: Parliament may declare major ports and aerodromes to be under Union control for specified purposes.

title: Article 365: Effect of failure to comply with, or to give effect to, directions given by the Union
excerpt: A state's failure to comply with Union directions is lawful ground for the President to hold that the state's government cannot run per the Constitution (a trigger for Article 356).

title: Article 366: Definitions
excerpt: Defines key terms used in the Constitution, such as 'agricultural income', 'estate duty', 'existing law' and 'railway'.

title: Article 367: Interpretation
excerpt: Applies the General Clauses Act, 1897 to the Constitution's interpretation unless the context otherwise requires.

title: Article 368: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor
excerpt: Parliament may amend the Constitution by special majority (two-thirds of members present and voting, with a majority of total membership); amendments affecting federal provisions need ratification by half the states; the

title: Article 369: Temporary power to Parliament to make laws with respect to certain matters in the State List as if they were matters in the Concurrent List
excerpt: Gave Parliament temporary (five-year) power over certain State List trade and commerce matters after commencement; long expired.

title: Article 370: Temporary provisions with respect to the State of Jammu and Kashmir
excerpt: Granted special status to Jammu and Kashmir with limited Union jurisdiction. In August 2019 it was substantially abrogated: C.O. 272 applied all constitutional provisions to J and K, and C.O. 273 declared Article 370 ino

title: Article 371: Special provision with respect to the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat
excerpt: The President may provide for separate development boards for Vidarbha, Marathwada, Saurashtra and Kutch, equitable allocation of funds, and technical education and employment opportunities.

title: Article 371A: Special provision with respect to the State of Nagaland
excerpt: Protects Naga customary law, religious and social practices, and land ownership from Parliamentary Acts unless the Assembly resolves otherwise; reserves Assembly seats and the Governor's special responsibility for law an

title: Article 371B: Special provision with respect to the State of Assam
excerpt: The President may provide for a committee of the Assembly comprising members from the tribal areas of Assam (22nd Amendment 1969).

title: Article 371C: Special provision with respect to the State of Manipur
excerpt: The President may provide for a committee of the Assembly comprising members from the hill areas of Manipur, with the Governor's special responsibility for its working (27th Amendment 1971).

title: Article 371D: Special provisions with respect to the State of Andhra Pradesh
excerpt: Provides for equitable opportunities in public employment and education through local cadres and the Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal (32nd Amendment 1973); after bifurcation, its application to Telangana was addre

title: Article 371E: Establishment of Central University in Andhra Pradesh
excerpt: Empowered Parliament to establish a Central University in Andhra Pradesh (32nd Amendment 1973; the University of Hyderabad was set up under it).

title: Article 371F: Special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim
excerpt: Protects Sikkim's pre-merger laws, reserves Assembly seats for different sections of the population, and gives the Governor special responsibility for peace and social advancement (36th Amendment 1975).

title: Article 371G: Special provision with respect to the State of Mizoram
excerpt: Protects Mizo customary law, religious and social practices, and land ownership from Parliamentary Acts unless the Assembly resolves otherwise (53rd Amendment 1986).

title: Article 371H: Special provision with respect to the State of Arunachal Pradesh
excerpt: Gives the Governor special responsibility for law and order in Arunachal Pradesh (55th Amendment 1986).

title: Article 371I: Special provision with respect to the State of Goa
excerpt: Reserves at least 30 seats in the Goa Assembly (56th Amendment 1986).

title: Article 371J: Special provision with respect to the State of Karnataka
excerpt: Provides for a separate development board for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, equitable fund allocation, and reservation in education and public employment for the region's residents (98th Amendment 2012).

title: Article 372: Continuance in force of existing laws and their adaptation
excerpt: Pre-Constitution laws continue in force until altered or repealed, subject to adaptation by the President's orders.

title: Article 372A: Power of the President to adapt laws
excerpt: Empowered the President to adapt laws for the 7th Amendment's state reorganisation by order before 1 November 1957.

title: Article 373: Power of President to make order in respect of persons under preventive detention in certain cases
excerpt: Empowered the President to order continued preventive detention of persons held under pre-Constitution provincial laws; long expired.

title: Article 374: Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council
excerpt: Transferred Federal Court judges to the Supreme Court and moved pending cases there at commencement.

title: Article 375: Courts, authorities and officers to continue to function subject to the provisions of the Constitution
excerpt: All pre-Constitution courts, authorities and officers continued to function subject to the Constitution.

title: Article 376: Provisions as to Judges of High Courts
excerpt: Deemed pre-Constitution High Court judges to be judges under the Constitution.

title: Article 377: Provisions as to Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
excerpt: Deemed the pre-Constitution Auditor-General of India to be the CAG under the Constitution.

title: Article 378: Provisions as to Public Service Commissions
excerpt: Deemed pre-Constitution Public Service Commissions (Federal and provincial) to be the UPSC and state PSCs under the Constitution.

title: Article 378A: Special provision as to duration of Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly
excerpt: Fixed the duration of the then-existing Andhra Pradesh Assembly (7th Amendment 1956); spent.

title: Article 379: Provisions as to provisional Parliament and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker thereof
excerpt: Provided for the Constituent Assembly to function as the provisional Parliament; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 380: Provision as to President
excerpt: Provided for the first President's election and term; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 381: Council of Ministers
excerpt: Provided for the first Council of Ministers; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 382: Provisions as to provisional Legislatures for States in Part A of the First Schedule
excerpt: Provided for provisional legislatures in Part A states; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 383: Provision as to Governors of Provinces
excerpt: Provided for the first Governors; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 384: Council of Ministers of Governors
excerpt: Provided for Governors' first Councils of Ministers; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 385: Provision as to provisional Legislatures in States in Part B of the First Schedule
excerpt: Provided for provisional legislatures in Part B states; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 386: Council of Ministers for States in Part B of the First Schedule
excerpt: Provided for Councils of Ministers in Part B states; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 387: Special provision as to determination of population for the purposes of certain elections
excerpt: Provided for population determination for early elections; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 388: Provisions as to the filling of casual vacancies in the provisional Parliament and provisional Legislatures of the States
excerpt: Provided for filling casual vacancies in provisional bodies; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 389: Provision as to Bills pending in the Dominion Legislature and in the Legislatures of Provinces and Indian States
excerpt: Provided for pending Bills at commencement; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 390: Money received or raised or expenditure incurred between the commencement of the Constitution and the 31st day of March, 1950
excerpt: Dealt with transitional finances for 1950; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 391: Power of the President to amend the First and Fourth Schedules in certain contingencies
excerpt: Empowered the President to amend the First and Fourth Schedules by order in contingencies; repealed by the 7th Amendment 1956.

title: Article 392: Power of the President to remove difficulties
excerpt: Empowers the President to remove difficulties in giving effect to the Constitution by order; in force and available for transitional difficulties.

title: Article 393: Short title
excerpt: This Constitution may be called the Constitution of India.

title: Article 394: Commencement
excerpt: Articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60, 324, 366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 came into force on 26 November 1949; the rest of the Constitution commenced on 26 January 1950.

title: Article 394A: Authoritative text in the Hindi language
excerpt: The President causes an authoritative Hindi translation of the Constitution to be published, with the same meaning as the English text (58th Amendment 1987).

title: Article 395: Repeals
excerpt: Repeals the Indian Independence Act, 1947 and the Government of India Act, 1935, with all enactments amending or supplementing them.
